common_name: Ensoro Ewia Eggplant (Ghanaian Ashanti Heirloom Scarlet Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; this Ashanti heirloom scarlet eggplant from Ghana tolerates drought and heat better than most Solanum melongena types, so it rewards a long, hot warm season.

directions: Ensoro Ewia is a drought- and heat-tolerant scarlet eggplant grown for generations by Ashanti farmers in Ghana, where seed keepers describe a history stretching back more than a century and a half. Start seed indoors and transplant into warm, fertile soil in full sun once nights stay reliably above 60F, since this African eggplant relative shrugs off prolonged heat that stresses standard garden eggplant. Plants build a sturdy, bushy frame and respond well to frequent picking; harvest fruit once it turns firm and reaches its full mature color, since lingering too long on the plant lets the flesh turn bitter and seedy. The line has grown scarce in its home region, so growing it out and saving seed helps keep this old Ghanaian strain in circulation.

common_name: Giant of Barman Eggplant (Madhya Pradesh Heirloom Giant Green-Striped Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; give this giant-fruited heirloom from Barman village in Madhya Pradesh extra room and sturdy support, since the elongated fruit can swell to several pounds.

directions: Giant of Barman is a heritage eggplant from the village of Barman along Madhya Pradesh's Narmada River, prized by local growers for fruit that can reach several pounds on a single plant. Transplant into deeply worked, fertile soil in full sun once the soil has warmed, and set sturdy stakes or a cage early, since the elongated green fruit with fine white pinstripes grows heavy enough to snap unsupported branches. The dense, sweet, comparatively seedless flesh holds up well to roasting and baking, so harvest while the skin is still glossy and keep watering consistent to prevent fruit from turning fibrous. Check plants every few days during peak season, since fruit size balloons quickly once pollinated and is best picked before it grows oversized.

common_name: Jewel Marble Eggplant (Compact Dwarf Marbled Violet-and-White Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before transplanting; the naturally compact, bushy habit makes Jewel Marble one of the better eggplants for large containers as well as small beds.

directions: Jewel Marble is a compact, dwarf eggplant bred for containers and small garden beds, producing an abundance of small fruit marbled in violet, mauve, and eggshell white with a glossy, almost lacquered finish. Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights are reliably warm, since the naturally tidy, bushy habit needs little pruning to stay productive in a pot. Pick fruit at about 2-3 inches across while the skin is still taut and shiny; the mild, nutty-sweet flesh is tender enough to roast whole or simmer into ratatouille without peeling. Frequent harvesting keeps these compact plants loaded with new flowers and fruit through a long summer.

common_name: Mitoyo Eggplant (Japanese Heirloom Near-Black Teardrop Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; Mitoyo is an old Japanese market variety traditionally grown around the Mitoyo and Kanonji districts and benefits from a full warm season to size up its teardrop fruit.

directions: Mitoyo is an old Japanese market eggplant traced to the Mitoyo and Kanonji districts, grown for oval, teardrop-shaped fruit that ripens to a deep, near-black purple. Transplant into warm, fertile soil in full sun once nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 55F, and keep the soil evenly moist to encourage the tender, sweet flesh the variety is known for. Harvest fruit at 4-6 inches long while the skin is still glossy; the flesh is mild enough to slice thin and eat raw, though it takes equally well to grilling, pickling, or classic Japanese nasu dishes. Regular picking keeps plants productive and prevents fruit from developing the bitterness and toughened skin of overripe eggplant.

common_name: Malaysian Dark Red Eggplant (Malaysian Heirloom Long Slender Violet Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; this rare Malaysian heirloom sets long, slender fruit best picked young and often through a long, hot growing season.

directions: Malaysian Dark Red is a rare heirloom eggplant from Malaysia, grown for long, slender fruit in a deep reddish-violet that darkens further as it matures. Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once the weather is reliably warm, allowing roughly 75 to 85 days from transplant to first harvest. The creamy, tender flesh carries a mild, faintly sweet flavor without the bitterness that affects many long Asian types, making it well suited to stir-fries, curries, and frying. Pick fruit while still glossy and firm at 6-8 inches long, and harvest frequently to keep plants setting new fruit through the season.

common_name: Kopec Eggplant (Indonesian-Type Heirloom Lilac-and-Purple Variegated Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before transplanting; Kopec descends from a USDA seed collection made in South Africa in 1956 but its variegated fruit points to the Indonesian 'kopek' eggplant tradition.

directions: Kopec is a rare eggplant preserved from a USDA germplasm collection made in South Africa in 1956, though its lilac-and-deep-purple variegated fruit points to roots in the Indonesian kopek eggplant tradition. Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm soil in full sun, giving plants 18-24 inches of spacing to branch out fully. Fruit size falls between a typical Japanese type and a globe eggplant, so harvest at 4-6 inches long and quarter it lengthwise for roasting to show off the marbled skin. Because it readily cross-pollinates with other eggplants, isolate plantings if you intend to save true-to-type seed.
